newsitem.title: UK: Argentina plans $2 bln global bond - London dealers.
newsitem.headline: Argentina plans $2 bln global bond - London dealers.

text.p: Argentina plans to launch a $2.0 billion global bond in two tranches with five- and 20-year maturities, syndicate managers said on Friday.
Merrill Lynch was tipped as lead manager but officials there declined to comment.
"Sovereigns with substantial financing requirements are looking to move quite early on in the year," said a syndicate manager at a U.S. bank.
"A $2.0 billion deal for Argentina is possibly their starting point. Mexico is also looking but there are no firm details on that yet," he said.
Some traders said Argentina could launch the deal as early as next week.
Others said no substantial issue was likely to emerge before next Friday's U.S. employment data, traders said, which were crucial to determining the direction of a jittery Treasuries.
A $1.0 billion five-year tranche for Argentina would be priced relative to outstanding Argentina 2001 and 2003 global bonds, bankers said.
Its 2001 paper was quoted at 288/280 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, and the 2003 bonds at 329/324 b.p. over.
For a 20-year maturity Mexico's 2016 global bond would be the benchmark. This was trading at 418/415 b.p. over Treasuries, dealers said, down from a 445 b.p. launch spread in September.
